figures.caption: Fig. 3. The geometry of the model: starting from an aver- age particle, with an average Voronoi cell (I), densification is modelled as concentric growth of the particle, beyond the stationary walls of its cell (new particle radius R’) (II). The excess volume outside the polyhedron (shaded) is redistributed either (a) evenly across the free surface of the sphere; this produces a truncated sphere of radius R” (‘compaction’ case. IIIa), or (b) near the contact region, forming necks (‘sintering’ case. Mb). Then the average area of contact between the particle and the cell walls are calcu- lated in each case. The coordination numbers are given by the RDF of the packing: G(2R”) and G(2R’), respectively.
